review_notes: I read the whole file and the AddMonoidAlgebra.scalarTensorEquiv / rTensorEquivAlgEquiv definitions. I grepped for uses of scalarRTensorAlgEquiv and algebraTensorAlgEquiv across Mathlib. The two defs have the same type up to renaming and the same body. The other declarations (rTensorAlgEquiv, tensorEquivSum, the IsPushout instances) are named specialisations of generic constructions, so I did not flag them. I did not check whether the module docstring's mentions of MvPolynomial.rTensor and scalarRTensor correspond to declarations that exist in Mathlib. The proposed consolidation is untested. The two defs have different explicit-argument conventions, which is a mild cost of the change.

findings.excerpt:
noncomputable def scalarRTensorAlgEquiv : N ⊗[R] MvPolynomial σ R ≃ₐ[N] MvPolynomial σ N :=
  AddMonoidAlgebra.scalarTensorEquiv R N
findings.problem: The file defines two independent declarations for the same equivalence `A ⊗[R] R[σ] ≃ₐ[A] A[σ]` for an `R`-algebra `A`. `scalarRTensorAlgEquiv` (with `N`) and `algebraTensorAlgEquiv R A` (lines 94–96) have the same statement up to renaming, and both are defined by `AddMonoidAlgebra.scalarTensorEquiv`. Only `algebraTensorAlgEquiv` gets API: `_tmul`, `_symm_X`, `_symm_monomial`, `_symm_map`. The `scalarRTensorAlgEquiv` copy has no simp lemmas. So its user in Spectrum/Prime/Polynomial.lean unfolds it by hand (`simp [scalarRTensorAlgEquiv, e, ...]`). Other files use the `algebraTensorAlgEquiv` copy and its lemmas. Users face two competing names, and the two equivalences are only defeq, not syntactically equal.
findings.proposed_change: Keep one declaration, probably `algebraTensorAlgEquiv`, which has the lemma API. Make `scalarRTensorAlgEquiv` a deprecated alias of it, or remove it and update Mathlib/RingTheory/Spectrum/Prime/Polynomial.lean to use `algebraTensorAlgEquiv R _` and its simp lemmas. Update the module docstring accordingly.
findings.benefit: This removes a redundant definition and lets the one remaining equivalence carry the whole lemma API. The Spectrum proof would no longer need to unfold the definition by hand. The docstring would also stop advertising two names for one concept.
